name: Thordata
summary: Proxy infrastructure and scraping stack: residential, mobile, ISP and datacenter proxies plus SERP/web-scraper APIs, priced per GB, IP or 1K requests.
best_for: data teams scraping at scale (price intelligence, SERP tracking, AI-training data) who want proxy infrastructure plus ready-made scraping APIs at aggressive per-unit rates
skip_if: you need predictable flat pricing, or your use case skirts site terms: residential proxying carries compliance questions no discount fixes
honest_knock: Everything is a meter (per GB, per IP, per 1K responses) so the bill scales with usage. And every rate the site advertises is the largest package on its ladder: $0.65 a GB means buying 5,000 GB, while 1 GB of the same product costs $2.00. Budget at your own volume, not at the headline. Plus the category-wide caveat we'd give any residential-proxy vendor: those '100M+ real residential IPs' come from consumer devices, so check sourcing ethics and your target sites' terms before building on it.

pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-09-23 against the vendor's own pricing page) (2026) Usage-metered, with free trials on the APIs. Every ladder is unchanged since 1 Sep 2026, and every advertised "from" rate is still the largest package on its ladder: residential $0.65/GB at 5,000 GB ($3,250) against $2.00/GB at 1 GB, $1.80 at 10 GB, $1.50 at 50 GB, $1.00 at 150 GB, $0.80 at 350 GB, $0.73 at 1,000 GB and $0.70 at 2,000 GB; mobile $2.20/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB; SERP API $0.70 per 1K at 1M responses against $1.20 at 15K; Web Scraper API $0.50 per 1K at 3M against $1.00 at 30K, with a 5,000-credit step the page's structured data prices at $0.00; the unblocker, now listed as "Webpage" (it was "Web Unlocker" on 1 Sep), $1.00 per 1K at 200K against $1.30 at 10K; Scraping Browser $2.50/GB at 500 GB against $5.00 at 1 GB. Static ISP and datacenter proxies advertise $0.75/IP against a $1.50 list, while the ISP packages themselves list at $1.50 and $4.50 an IP. New on the page: High Bandwidth Proxies sold by time, not volume -- 1 day $280, 7 days $900, 30 days $2,370, 60 days $4,140 -- with no bandwidth or IP count stated. The residential rows up to 350 GB carry struck 'original' prices ($2.85, $2.75, $1.95, $1.50, $1.70) that do not form a ladder: the struck price at 350 GB is higher than at 150 GB. The card grid lower on the page prints SERP at $0.80 per 1K while the menu and the ladder say $0.70. Refund policy: within 7 days of the first purchase of a product, only if no more than 30% of the package and no more than 2 GB has been used, not for crypto payments, and not once a bundle bought in the dashboard has started transmitting data; an expired package period is not refundable.

price_history.method: Stable = every amount on the vendor's pricing page identical across >= 3 of our reads over >= 30 days. A change is listed only after we confirmed the new price on the page, with a verbatim quote. Differences in raw readings are never published on their own.

measured.tested_by: Our team; actor, account and scope are documented in the review.
method: The test used an account we made, and our AI assistant ran it in our browser; the free Webpage trial was claimed without KYC, card or phone number; nothing was bought and nothing was paid

claims.observed: Webpage, Pricing, Start with Trial: 3 clicks and about 1 minute, with an order summary of 500 for 7 Days at $0 and no KYC, card or phone number asked; the Overview showed Wallet $0.000. The dossier only says free API trials.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The trial claim in the dossier against the trial that was claimed; the dossier names no trial size or length.
claims.buying_consequence: A free trial of the Webpage API exists and needs no card, so you can try it without paying.

claims.observed: Every one of the 8 answers carried "credits":2, and the balance went from 500 to 484, so 16 for 8 requests. The 500 of the trial are therefore about 250 requests.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The trial size in the order summary against the credits that the answers took from the balance.
claims.buying_consequence: The trial gives half the requests that the headline number suggests.

claims.claim: The advertised rate looks cheap, but my first project is nowhere near the size that earns it.
claims.observed: A first project can start at 1 GB for $2, but the rate falls from $2 per GB to $0.65 per GB only at 5,000 GB for $3250, so a small first project pays the high rates.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The tier list in the plan pages against the pain in the dossier; no proxy traffic was bought, so real project costs were not measured.
claims.buying_consequence: You can start small for $2, but the low per-GB rates need a volume that a first project does not reach.

claims.observed: Own calculation: the Webpage API charges per answer ($1.30 per 1K at the 10,000 pack), so for answers of 3636 bytes it comes to about $361 per GB, and about $722 per GB counting 2 credits per answer, against $2 per GB for residential. Larger real pages lower the figure; the dashboard shows no gigabytes.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: Our own arithmetic on 8 test answers against the per-GB price; the vendor shows no per-GB figure for this product.
claims.buying_consequence: For small pages the per-answer Webpage API is far more expensive per GB than residential traffic; for larger pages it gets cheaper per GB.

claims.observed: The httpbin answers showed an outgoing IP address together with a User-Agent and a From header that identify Googlebot. This is a plain observation; the cause was not investigated and other target sites were not tried.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The httpbin /headers answer against no dossier claim on the identity of the requests.
claims.buying_consequence: The requests did not show an ordinary browser identity; check what your own target sites see before you rely on it.

claims.observed: The Statistics tab showed 8 successful, 0 failed and an average time of 0.38 seconds, and no gigabytes. Our own measure of the answers was 97 to 3636 bytes.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The count in the dashboard against our own 8 requests; the bandwidth could not be compared.
claims.buying_consequence: You pay per answer and the dashboard counts answers, so measure the size of your own pages yourself.

claims.observed: The residential tiers were 1 GB $2/GB (total $2), 10 GB $1.8/GB ($18), 50 GB $1.5/GB ($75), 150 GB $1/GB ($150) and 350 GB $0.8/GB ($280), with $2.85, $2.75, $1.95, $1.5 and $1.7 per GB struck through; the minimum purchase is 1 GB. The same numbers are in the dossier and were seen again on the public page.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The five tiers in the dashboard against the dossier and the public page; no tax was shown.
claims.buying_consequence: The residential prices have not changed against the dossier.

claims.observed: The order summary for 350 GB showed Price before discount $595, 55% Discount -$315 and Total $280. The public page shows no discount percentage and no price before discount.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The order summary against the dossier, which has no discount line; our own division of the discount is in the README.
claims.buying_consequence: The $280 for 350 GB is presented as a 55% discount; the discount line is new against the dossier.

claims.observed: The Enterprise rows were 1,000 GB $0.73/GB = $730, 2,000 GB $0.7/GB = $1400 and 5,000 GB $0.65/GB = $3250, the same as in the dossier; above that the page says Contact sales.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The three Enterprise rows against the dossier rows; nothing was bought.
claims.buying_consequence: The big-volume rates are unchanged and need at least 1,000 GB.

claims.observed: Right after the trial was claimed, the page behind the message showed Total $13 with Continue to checkout for the 10,000 pack. It was not clicked.
claims.plan: Free Webpage trial; the plan pages and the order summary were viewed, nothing was paid
claims.comparability: The upsell on screen against the free claim that had just been completed; the checkout was not opened.

claims.comparability: The account page against a test that stayed on the free Webpage trial and did not buy residential traffic.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested the free Webpage trial of Thordata: 500 answers for 7 days at $0, claimed in 3 clicks in about a minute with no KYC, card or phone number. Every answer took 2 credits, so the balance went from 500 to 484 after 8 requests, about 250 requests in all, all HTTP 200. The dashboard counts answers and shows no gigabytes; by our own calculation from 3636 byte test pages the Webpage API comes to about $361 per GB, or about $722 per GB counting the 2 credits, against $2 per GB for residential. The httpbin answers showed a Googlebot identity (observation only). The residential prices are unchanged against the dossier ($2 per GB for 1 GB down to $0.65 per GB at 5,000 GB); the order summary of 350 GB now shows Price before discount $595 and 55% Discount -$315. Nothing was bought and the payment screen was not opened. Account and start: the account was created by us (registration 18/11/2026, dashboard.thordata.com, interface already in English); our AI assistant ran the test in our Chrome from about 14:35 (Amsterdam). The Overview showed Wallet $0.000 and the trial token was valid until 25/11/2026. No KYC, card or phone number was asked for the trial. The dossier name is Thordata and the review is on AIBM (b2b/thordata-review). The pain that was tested: Teams starting a first scraping project, "The advertised rate looks cheap, but my first project is nowhere near the size that earns it." (dossier: solved in part, no alternative listed). Core action: Webpage, Pricing, the Webpage pack of 500 answers for 7 days at $0, Start with Trial. The order summary said 500 for 7 Days and $0, the message was Successfully claimed the trial! with the button Go use it: 3 clicks, about 1 minute. Right after the claim the page behind it showed Total $13 with Continue to checkout (the 10,000 pack); it was not clicked. Playground: the balance said 500 with Expiration time 25/11/2026, and the example is a cURL POST to the Webunlocker endpoint with a Bearer token (the token is not recorded anywhere). 8 requests were sent, only to httpbin (/ip, /headers and /html), all HTTP 200 in 0.4 to 0.75 seconds. Every answer carried "credits":2. The answers were 97, 374 and 3636 bytes, 15,487 bytes in total. Observation, no judgment: the httpbin answers showed an outgoing IP address and a User-Agent and a From header that identify Googlebot (googlebot(at)googlebot.com). The cause was not investigated and whether a normal target site sees the same was not tested. Statistics: Total usage 8, successful 8, failed 0, average response time 0.38 seconds; the dashboard shows no gigabytes for the Webpage API. The balance fell from 500 to 484, so 16 for 8 requests, 2 per answer, which leaves about 250 requests in the trial. After the 8 requests the API token was refreshed in the dashboard (Refresh, Confirm, Refresh successfully); a 9th request with the old key gave {"code":401,"data":"API key authentication failed:API Token is error"}. 9 requests in all, within the limit of 20. The new token was not viewed or recorded. Own calculation, not a vendor figure: the Webpage API is priced per answer, the dashboard shows no gigabytes, and the tester measured the size of the answers himself: 97, 374 and 3636 bytes, 15,487 bytes in all for 8 requests (15.487 in the raw note, a Dutch thousands dot). At $1.30 per 1K for the 10,000 pack, a page of the largest test size (3636 bytes, about 3,6 KB) is 3,6 MB per 1K answers, which is about $361 per GB. Because every answer took 2 credits from the balance, the reading with credits is about $722 per GB. Residential Proxies cost $2 per GB at the 1 GB tier, far below that. The figure only holds for pages as small as the httpbin test pages; real pages are larger, so the cost per GB of the Webpage API would drop in proportion, and whether a credit costs the price of an answer or half of it was not verified. The 8 test requests are too small a sample for more. Plans, up to the point of paying: Residential Proxies, tab Regular, pay-as-you-go, never expires, read by the tester in the dashboard on 18 Nov 2026: 1 GB $2/GB ($2.85/GB struck through), total $2 (tag New Users); 10 GB $1.8/GB, total $18; 50 GB $1.5/GB, total $75; 150 GB $1/GB, total $150; 350 GB $0.8/GB, total $280 (tag Best price). The order summary for 350 GB shows validity 30 Days, Price before discount $595, 55% Discount -$315 and Total $280. Enterprise, never expires: 1,000 GB $0.73/GB = $730; 2,000 GB $0.7/GB = $1400; 5,000 GB $0.65/GB = $3250; above that Custom Pricing Based on Demand / Contact sales. The minimum purchase is 1 GB ($2). Tax was not shown before checkout and the payment screen was not opened; card and crypto icons were visible. Webpage API, per answer: 10,000 answers $1.30/1K = $13; 50,000 $1.20/1K = $60; 100,000 $1.10/1K = $110; 200,000 $1.00/1K = $200. The public page thordata.com/pricing/residential-proxies was read again just before this delivery the same day and shows the same five Regular tiers (1 GB $2.00, 10 GB $1.80, 50 GB $1.50, 150 GB $1.00, 350 GB $0.80 per GB; totals $2.00, $18.00, $75.00, $150.00, $280.00; struck through $2.85, $2.75, $1.95, $1.50, $1.70), the High Volume rows (1000 GB $730.00, 2000 GB $1400.00, 5000 GB $3250.00) and the same Webpage packs. So the prices are unchanged against the dossier. Only the 55% discount line is new: it appears in the order summary of the dashboard, and the public page shows no discount percentage and no price before discount. The refund rule was not tested. Cancelling: Avatar, My Account, Account Settings has a Delete Account button with the text that the service is deactivated immediately after deletion; it was not clicked. The same page shows Account verification (KYC) Not verified with a Verify account button; it was not clicked, so whether Residential Proxies need the verification is unknown. Not tested: the residential proxies themselves (not bought, no proxy traffic), a refund, tax and the payment screen, where the IP addresses come from, the KYC rule for residential, and bandwidth in GB for the Webpage API. Clean up: the account, the trial (484 answers left until 25/11/2026) and the new token stay; there is no wallet balance and nothing was bought; our own tab was closed, no other tab was touched; no login details were saved in files. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free Webpage trial is smaller than it looks: every answer takes 2 credits, so 500 gives about 250 requests. The dashboard counts answers and not gigabytes, so you cannot compare the Webpage API with the per-GB prices of residential traffic without measuring your own page sizes; for pages as small as our test pages it comes out far more expensive per GB. The low per-GB rates need volume: $2 per GB at 1 GB and $0.65 per GB only at 5,000 GB. Our httpbin answers showed a Googlebot identity, so check what your own target sites see. The account page shows KYC as not verified; whether residential needs it was not tested.
